issues.label: Recession
issues.summary: Sustained contraction in economic output characterized by declining GDP, rising unemployment, falling consumer spending, and business investment pullback, often triggering cascading effects across sectors

circuits.detail: GDP output contracting as productive capacity sits idle and aggregate demand falls below potential
Labor markets seizing up with rising unemployment, reduced hours, and declining participation rates
Consumer spending retreating as households cut discretionary purchases and increase precautionary saving
Industrial production declining as factories reduce shifts and defer capital investment
Entrepreneurial activity suppressed as risk capital dries up and startup formation declines

issues.label: Hyperinflation
issues.summary: Extreme and accelerating price increases destroying the purchasing power of currency, eroding savings, collapsing real wages, and threatening the viability of monetary exchange itself

circuits.detail: Price-level homeostasis completely broken with exponential increases in general price level
Monetary policy transmission mechanism breaking down as conventional interest rate tools lose effectiveness
Fiscal discipline collapsed with government deficits being monetized through currency printing
Consumer behavior shifting to panic buying and immediate spending as holding currency becomes irrational
Debt markets in crisis as lenders demand extreme risk premiums or refuse to lend in devaluing currency
International trade partners withdrawing from commercial relationships denominated in the collapsing currency

issues.label: Banking Crisis
issues.summary: Systemic failure in the banking sector through insolvency, liquidity crises, or loss of depositor confidence, threatening the payment system and credit intermediation functions essential to economic activity

circuits.detail: Banking system executive functions paralyzed as institutions hoard cash and refuse to lend
Fear contagion spreading through debt markets as counterparty risk assessments trigger cascading credit freezes
Monetary policy transmission completely blocked as interest rate cuts fail to reach the real economy through frozen banks
Capital market pricing distorted as asset valuations become disconnected from fundamentals during panic
Real estate markets collapsing as foreclosures spike and property values plummet from credit withdrawal

issues.label: Trade War
issues.summary: Escalating cycle of retaliatory tariffs, sanctions, and trade barriers between major economies, disrupting global supply chains, raising consumer prices, and fragmenting the international trading system

circuits.detail: Perspective-taking between trading partners collapsed, replaced by zero-sum confrontational framing
Supply chains thrown into chaos as firms scramble to reroute around tariff barriers and sanctions
Industrial production disrupted by input cost increases and lost export markets, with some sectors benefiting from protection while others suffer
Import price inflation feeding through to consumer prices as tariffs raise costs of foreign goods
Regulatory complexity exploding as compliance requirements multiply across fragmented trade regimes
Technology sector innovation slowing as cross-border research collaboration and component access restricted

issues.label: Debt Crisis
issues.summary: Unsustainable accumulation of sovereign or corporate debt threatening default, requiring painful restructuring, and potentially triggering contagion across interconnected financial systems

circuits.detail: Debt market fear spiraling as bond yields spike and credit default swap spreads widen to crisis levels
Fiscal policy space exhausted with debt service consuming increasing share of government revenue
Banking system destabilized as sovereign or corporate bond holdings face mark-to-market losses
Economic indicators sending contradictory signals as traditional metrics fail to capture debt dynamics
Monetary policy constrained between need to raise rates for inflation and fear of worsening debt burden

issues.label: Market Crash
issues.summary: Sudden and severe decline in asset prices across equity, bond, and commodity markets, destroying wealth, triggering margin calls, and potentially cascading into broader economic contraction

circuits.detail: Capital market risk evaluation overwhelmed by panic selling and herd behavior, rational pricing abandoned
Fear contagion amplifying sell-offs as loss aversion and margin calls create self-reinforcing downward spirals
Consumer confidence collapsing as household wealth destruction from portfolio losses suppresses spending
Real estate values declining as wealth effect reversal and credit tightening reduce property demand
Entrepreneurial and venture capital activity freezing as risk appetite evaporates across investor classes
Regulatory response scrambling with emergency interventions and ad hoc rule changes adding uncertainty
